title: First completion of a nonempty row load
statement: Let $l>0$, let $x$ be a binary input word, and let $p$ be an input-head position for $x$. Suppose $old$ and $new$ assign a binary word to each of the $l$ fields, with old-word lengths at most $U$ and new-word lengths at most $W$. For any binary prefix and trailer, the row loader started at field zero with the old fields and the stream containing the prefix, packed new fields, and trailer reaches the complete-row configuration at some time $t$ with $0<t\le l(2U+3W+7)$, and at every earlier time $j<t$ its state is not the complete-row control at field index $l$.
hypotheses_covered: old and new assign words to the $l$ fields
each old word has length at most $U$
each new word has length at most $W$
replaced: For a positive field count, every input word, input position, old fields of length at most $U$, new fields of length at most $W$, and stream prefix and trailer, there is a strictly positive time $t \le l\,(2U + 3W + 7)$ at which the row loader first reaches its complete-row return, holding the new row with all heads restored and the exact sequential stream cursor.
